Open upstream explanations: SOC estimation / calibration error; Usable capacity far below the stated parameter; Current under-measured or load bypassing the sensor. safety_findings.statement: Do not close HV or charge until every cell's rest voltage is assessed; the lowest cell reached 2.421 V during reclosure, below the original trip level.
Three HV reclosures after a protective shutdown; the cells were discharged below the original trip level. Over-discharge risk needs a trained technician.
HV was closed three times after the protective shutdown at 2100.5 s (3266.5, 3320.8, 3404.5 s). Whether that was permitted depends on a restart policy not in the data.
Each of the three closures ended in another protective shutdown (closed 3266.5 s, tripped 3285.0 s; closed 3320.8 s, tripped 3339.3 s; closed 3404.5 s, tripped 3422.5 s). Do not retry closing HV.
The three closures followed a fault reset the record does not show (it fell in a gap). Who or what reset the fault is unknown.
9 escalations, highest level 3, are recorded. There is no protection specification to judge the sequence against, so it is not judged as correct or incorrect.

unknowns: Why the SOC was overstated, or whether capacity or current sensing is wrong; the recording cannot separate these
Calibration history since the last full charge, and the BMS under-voltage thresholds and delays
What commanded the HV reclosures at 3266.5, 3320.8 and 3404.5 s; only contactor feedback is recorded
